A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, figures and appendices. The complete 28-page v2 and 32-page v3 support reliable comparison, including matching material moved into v3's appendices.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figure 3 report original experiments measuring learned OT-map errors on two- and four-dimensional Gaussian-mixture problems across training sample sizes.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original convergence experiment and adds original results from varying potential-network and transport-network widths in Figure 4.

M1.justification: The semi-dual minimax objective, learned potential and transport map, and ICNN/MLP components remain unchanged. The added width sweep evaluates model configurations without introducing a new algorithm or component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate quadratic OT on the same two- and four-dimensional Gaussian-mixture benchmark. The added experiment changes sample size and network capacity within this coverage; newly discussed image and biological applications are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical comparisons against competing OT solvers. Figure 4 compares configurations of the existing solver, while additional cited methods appear only in discussion.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 introduces a separate protocol using approximately 10 million benchmark samples, potential widths from 4 to 64 and transport-map widths from 1 to 8. This complements the retained sample-size sweep from 100 to 20,000; it does not replace that experiment's settings.

E4.justification: The new Section 5.2/Figure 4 studies sensitivity to potential and transport-network capacity, using abundant data to reduce estimation error. This adds a focused empirical examination of approximation error beyond v2's sample-size analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars for its experiments. Figure 4 adds point estimates without changing uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Figure 3 is identical, retaining fitted slopes of -0.728 for dimension 2 and -0.502 for dimension 4. Figure 4 adds results showing generally decreasing map error with greater network capacity, including nonmonotonic behavior in dimension 2. These are new configuration-dependent results, not improvements under the original settings.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 changes intermediate map bounds from L2(p) to L1(p) and corrects Lemma A.6's argument. Appendix A.4 replaces Lemma A.9's proof and changes Lemma A.12's covering radius from epsilon/(2L) to epsilon/(4L). Appendix A.5 replaces the zero-mean, independent-coordinate calculation with compact-support moment bounds. These revise supporting mathematics while retaining the main theorem statements and convergence rates.

C1.justification: The abstract and main contributions retain the same error decomposition, Rademacher-complexity bounds, approximation guarantees and learnability claims for quadratic minimax OT solvers. The added experiment supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly acknowledges the absence of practical guidance for selecting network hyperparameters and qualifies some results as closer to consistent estimation theory. Section 5.2 interprets the capacity results while acknowledging optimization-related outliers; Appendix B adds discussion of practical relevance.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 newly discloses the retained experiment's maximum transport-network width of 512 and the benchmark potential's width of 64. It also documents the new width ranges, while Appendix C specifies a batch size of 1024 for the added experiment. Existing optimizer, training-budget, hardware and test-sample disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds targeted coverage of out-of-sample OT estimators, neural-network capacity bounds, ICNN applications and practical OT uses. It also expands the explanation of GAN-versus-OT objectives in Appendix D. The existing GAN literature review is retained there, and the central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 moves the GAN discussion from Section 3.2 to Appendix D, divides the experiments into Sections 5.1 and 5.2, and adds focused explanatory passages and an LLM-usage disclosure. Terminology, affiliations and prose receive edits, while most background and theoretical exposition remain closely matched.

P2.justification: v3 adds the two-panel Figure 4 with legends for potential widths and curves across transport widths. Figures 1–3 retain identical image content. The document also changes title/author formatting, heading typography and running headers, with accompanying text reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 improves mathematical support through concrete appendix corrections, particularly replacing the extra coordinate assumptions in Appendix A.5 with compact-support bounds. The capacity experiment and clearer limitations add useful evidence and transparency. The gains remain limited: the principal results are unchanged, and the new experiment remains an illustrative study whose interpretation can be affected by optimization error.
